subject: SLA coverage split, credit schedule and attestation request
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@uptide.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samuel Park <sam.park@uptide.com>, Uptide Legal <legal@uptide.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Review: Redwood SLA template — coverage split and credits

Ben / Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the draft SLA. Our procurement and legal teams did a first pass (see attached "uptide_review_notes.pdf") and we have three asks we want to surface before redlines: 

1) Coverage split — we operate a hybrid setup: Uptide will use Redwood hosted for development and a dedicated cluster for production. We need the SLA to explicitly cover the dedicated cluster at a higher uptime threshold than the hosted tier (we propose 99.95% for dedicated, 99.9% hosted).

2) Credit caps and cadence — we prefer a monthly credit scheme that scales with the size of the outage rather than a flat cap tied to number of incidents. Our guideline: credits up to 10% of that month’s invoice for sustained outages > 2 hours.

3) Latency SLOs — we need a p95 latency target for inference on the dedicated pool (suggested 250ms p95) and a clear measurement endpoint & method for measuring p95.

Also, two smaller items: 
- A maintenance attestation: we need a weekly maintenance calendar for the dedicated cluster and a promised notice window (48 hours) for planned maintenance.
- Carveouts: cold-start/model-rollout warm-ups should not be treated as availability incidents, but we want the warm-up window to be capped (e.g., 30 minutes per rollout).

Can you confirm which of these items Redwood is willing to accept in principle so we can route to legal for redlines?

Attachments: uptide_review_notes.pdf

Best,
Elena Cruz
Head of Procurement, Uptide Financial

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@uptide.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 18:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Review: Redwood SLA template — coverage split and credits

Elena,

Really helpful — thanks for the clear asks and the annotated PDF. Quick response on Redwood's position so we can unblock legal: 

- Coverage split: we can support a dual-tiered SLA in contract language. Our standard offering would be: hosted API at 99.9% (monthly credit tiers), dedicated reserved cluster at 99.95%. We will include language that allows you to pin a model version to the dedicated pool for production workloads.

- Credits: we prefer a tiered credit schedule tied to aggregate monthly downtime rather than single-incident caps. Tentative proposal (open to negotiation):
  * Dedicated cluster: 99.95%–99.9% = 5% monthly credit, 99.9%–99.0% = 10% credit, below 99.0% escalate to executive review
  * Hosted: 99.9%–99.0% = 5% credit, below 99.0% further review
  We can map these to invoice percentages; if Uptide wants an absolute 10% upper bound on credits per month, we can accommodate that as a hard cap.

- Latency SLO: we can commit to a p95 for inference on the dedicated pool. Recommended initial number from infra is 250ms p95 for 512-token workloads; we need to define the measurement endpoint (we propose a dedicated /health/metrics endpoint that returns p95 over a rolling 30d window, with telemetry fed to both parties).

- Maintenance notice & attestation: we can provide a scheduled maintenance calendar for the dedicated cluster and commit to >=48h notice for planned maintenance that affects production. For urgent maintenance we will notify ASAP and provide a post-mortem.

- Cold-start carveout: agree in principle to carve out a warm-up window. SE suggested cap: 30 minutes per major model rollout; for repeated rollouts we can specify an aggregated cap per month. Karthik, can you confirm the technical feasibility and proposed wording?

I'm attaching our current SLA template for clarity: redwood_sla_template_v2.2.pdf. If Uptide is comfortable with the dual-tier structure outlined above, we can ask legal to prepare a tracked redline and circulate.

Next step: let me know if the credit cap of 10% is a hard requirement. If yes, we'll insert the cap in the draft and loop in our finance/legal teams.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Review: Redwood SLA template — coverage split and credits

Elena / Ben,

Technical notes from SE perspective: 

- Measurement & p95: we can surface a p95 metric via our telemetry pipeline for the dedicated cluster. Important definition note: p95 will be computed over successful inference responses, excluding error responses and external network time. We'll publish the exact measurement interval and method in the SLA (rolling 30-day window, daily snapshots).

- Cold-start / model-rollout carveout: agree to carve out warm-up behavior but recommend tighter bounds — 30 minutes per model rollout, with a maximum of 90 minutes aggregated per calendar month across rollouts. This prevents exploitation via repeated rollouts.

- Warm-up identification: we propose a tagging mechanism (model:rollout=true) that Uptide's deploy process can include; Redwood's monitoring will treat tag-based traffic as warm-up if the tag is present for the first 30 minutes. If Uptide cannot add tags, we'll rely on rollout timestamps and heuristic detection (e.g., sudden increase in cache misses) with a log of identified warm-ups shared in post-mortems.

- Measurement endpoint: we recommend a read-only metrics endpoint (metrics.uptide.redwood/v1/p95) accessible via mTLS and a shared API key for correlation. This will allow Uptide to independently verify p95. If Uptide prefers, we can provide periodic exports to a shared S3 bucket.

I'll prepare suggested SLA language for the carveout and measurement definitions and circulate later today. Ben — if Uptide is okay with the 10% monthly cap as a negotiation anchor, say so and I'll include it in the draft wording.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: uptide_proposed_edits.docx (internal copy)
